Ballylinny Civil Parish

Guide to **Ballylinny Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland ancestry, family history, and genealogy**. Parish registers, transcripts, baptism records, marriage records, and burial records.

## Historical Overview

### History

The parish of Ballylinny is in the poor law union of Antrim, barony of Lower Belfast. It adjoins the town of Ballyclare. The living is a vicarage, in the diocese of Connor, united to the vicarage of Carmoney and the rectory of Ballymartin. The church was destroyed but the churchyard is still used as a graveyard by the parishioners.

The Presbyterians have a place of worship here.

In the Roman Catholic divisions the parish is part of the district of Larne and Carrickfergus.

### Localities

A list of the names of town-lands in this civil parish can be obtained at website: [www.seanruad.com](http://www.thecore.com/seanruad).

The surrounding parishes are: Ballymartin, Ballynure, Carnmoney, Grange of Doagh, and Templepatrick.

### Maps and gazetteers

* See [Ireland Maps](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Maps "Ireland Maps") and [Ireland Gazetteers](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Gazetteers "Ireland Gazetteers") for more information.

### Cemeteries

The townland of Ballylinny has two graveyards one is Presbyterian the other is not stated. There is also in the townland of Ballymartin a graveyard.

### Census

* See [Ireland Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Census "Ireland Census") for more information.

### Church records

* See [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records "Ireland Church Records") for more information.

#### Catholic

The Roman Catholics living in the civil parish have a meeting place in Ballyclare. The parish is part of Ballyclare and part of Carrickfergus in the diocese of Connor.

Ballyclare's earliest register for baptisms is July 1869 and for marriages February 1870. The registers are in the custody of the local church and the National Library of Ireland has a microfilmed copy of them. The records have been indexed by the Ulster Historical Foundation.

#### Church of Ireland

As stated above the church was destroyed in Ballylinny, parishioners meet at theCarnmoney parish church. The registers in Carnmoney begin as follows: baptisms: 1788; marriages 1789; deaths: 1845.

The original registers are in the custody of the local church and microfilm copies are available at the FamilySearch Library in Salt Lake City, Utah and at FamilySearch Centers around the world. The film numbers are: 990097 or another copy is on film 990488 (baptisms cover 1788 through 1879; marriages and deaths cover 1791 through 1855).

#### Presbyterian

The Presbyterian population in Ballylinny attended church in Ballyclare and church registers begin for both baptisms and marriages in 1837.

The original register are in the custody of the local church. Microfilm copies of these records can be found at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) film number MIC 1P/327 (1851-); FamilySearch Library in Salt Lake City, Utah film number 973220 (cover baptisms/marriages from 1837) film numbers 883875-883884 contain an index to the records).

The Presbyterian register of Antrim are being indexed by the Ulster Historical Foundation.

#### Others

### Civil Registration

Government registration of births and deaths began in 1864. Registration of Protestant marriages began in 1845, with all marriages being registered by 1864.

* See [Ireland Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Civil_Registration "Ireland Civil Registration") for more information.

### Tax records

The valuation of property for tax purposes was started in the 1840s by Richard Griffith. A tax paid to the church, call Tithe Applotments, began in the 1820s. Read about these records in the [Ireland Taxation](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Taxation "Ireland Taxation") and [Ireland Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Land_and_Property "Ireland Land and Property") articles.
